stories.title: HMRC Collects Record £227.7 Billion in Q1 2026
stories.summary: HMRC collected £227.7 billion in tax between April and June 2026, £16.6 billion more than the same period last year — without any headline tax rises. The surge reflects strong economic activity and tightened compliance measures.

stories.title: HMRC's New 'Sanctionable Conduct' Powers Could Impact Conveyancers
stories.summary: HMRC is introducing new 'sanctionable conduct' powers that could affect conveyancers and tax advisers. A first offence carries a penalty of between £7,500 and £1 million, with details of non-compliant advisers to be published on GOV.UK.

stories.title: House of Lords Criticises Proposed ILR Qualifying Period Extension
stories.summary: A House of Lords committee has said that extending the Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) qualifying period from 5 years to 10 years for people already in the UK would be unfair. The proposed change has been a controversial part of the government's immigration overhaul.

stories.title: Home Office Rejects Palestinian Jerusalemite Woman's UK Visa While Approving Husband's
stories.summary: The Home Office has rejected a UK visa application from a Palestinian woman from Jerusalem while approving her husband's, raising questions about inconsistency in immigration decision-making.

stories.title: Major UK Immigration Report Published — Could Reshape Visa Sponsorship
stories.summary: A major immigration report has been published that could reshape visa sponsorship opportunities for thousands of skilled workers, with potential implications for employer sponsorship licences and workforce planning.

stories.title: Iran Warns UK Over Use of British Military Bases in Recent Attacks
stories.summary: Iran has formally warned the United Kingdom over the alleged use of British military bases in recent operations, calling the actions a violation of international law and declaring British bases legitimate military targets.

stories.title: FCDO Updates Travel Advice for Multiple Countries
stories.summary: The Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office has issued updated travel advice for several countries including Italy, Uganda, and Algeria, where it continues to advise against all travel to parts of the country.

stories.title: New PM Burnham Faces £300bn Welfare Bill Challenge
stories.summary: New Prime Minister Andy Burnham faces pressure to cut the £300 billion welfare bill if he wants to fund his spending plans, with the Telegraph reporting that tough decisions on benefits reform are unavoidable.

stories.title: Benefits Reform Debate Intensifies as Opposition Challenges Government Approach
stories.summary: Opposition MPs are criticising the new government's approach to welfare spending, arguing that letting the welfare bill 'run wild' is not compassionate and puts future support for those who need it at risk.

stories.title: New Anchoring Restrictions at Allonby to Protect Marine Ecosystems
stories.summary: New rules coming into effect on 30 July will restrict where boats can drop anchor at Allonby, as part of efforts to protect fragile underwater ecosystems in the area.

stories.title: Sir Harold Hillier Gardens Named DEFRA Bees' Needs Champion for 2026
stories.summary: Sir Harold Hillier Gardens has been named one of DEFRA's Bees' Needs Champions for 2026, recognising its work in boosting biodiversity and helping nature recovery across its grounds.

stories.title: World's Deepest Vertical Farm Launches 1.1km Underground Near Whitby
stories.summary: Urban Crop Solutions has launched the world's deepest vertical farm inside a working mine near Whitby, testing whether crops can be grown commercially underground. The project has implications for UK food security and rural land use policy.

stories.title: UK Approves US Military Operations from RAF Fairford; Iran Threatens British Bases
stories.summary: New PM Andy Burnham has approved the continued use of British military bases (including RAF Fairford) for US operations against Iran. Iran has responded by declaring British military bases legitimate targets, significantly raising tensions.

stories.title: UK Cancels Military Exercise in Kenya
stories.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence has cancelled a planned military exercise in Kenya. The MoD said it 'highly values its relationship with Kenya, which is underpinned by mutual benefit, respect and cooperation,' though gave no specific reason for the cancellation.

stories.title: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting Sets Out Military Investment and Modernisation Plans
stories.summary: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting has outlined a programme of investment and modernisation for the UK's armed forces, covering improvements to kit, accommodation, and support for serving personnel and veterans.

stories.title: India-UK Free Trade Agreement Takes Effect — 99% Market Access for Indian Exporters
stories.summary: The India-UK Free Trade Agreement has come into force in July 2026, granting 99% access for Indian exporters to the UK market. The deal is one of the most significant bilateral trade agreements the UK has signed since Brexit.

stories.title: UK Government Appoints First Ever Minister for Artificial Intelligence
stories.summary: Kanishka Narayan MP has been appointed as the UK's first Minister for Artificial Intelligence to sit at the cabinet table, a role based at the Department for Business and Trade. The move signals a major elevation of AI policy in the new Burnham government.

agencies.name: DSIT
agencies.description: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology

stories.title: Lord Vallance Appointed Chair of PM's New AI Taskforce
stories.summary: Lord Vallance has been appointed chair of the Prime Minister's new AI Taskforce, which reports directly to PM Andy Burnham. AI Minister Kanishka Narayan will lead the unit, representing a major structural shift in how AI policy is governed at the heart of government.

stories.title: DSIT Publishes Response to 'Growing Up in an Online World' Consultation
stories.summary: DSIT has published additional details of measures it will take in response to the 'Growing Up in an Online World' consultation, sitting alongside Ofcom's Category 1 online safety proposals for major platforms.

stories.title: Andy Burnham Becomes UK Prime Minister — Major Shift for NHS Policy
stories.summary: Andy Burnham, former Health Secretary with strong NHS ties, has become the new UK Prime Minister. BBC's Laura Kuenssberg was given unprecedented behind-the-scenes access to Burnham's first days in power at Downing Street.

stories.title: Nurse Completes Historic 50-Year Career at the Same NHS Hospital
stories.summary: Kim Helm has completed her final shift as a children's nurse after a 50-year career — having watched the hospital she worked in being built before joining it as staff. The story highlights the long-term dedication of NHS workers.

stories.title: T-Pro Acquires BigHand Healthcare, Expanding NHS Digital Partnership
stories.summary: T-Pro has acquired BigHand Healthcare in July 2026, creating a combined organisation that works with approximately 120 NHS trusts. The merger strengthens the digital health ecosystem supporting NHS clinical documentation and workflow.

stories.title: Royal Mail Stamp Prices Rising — First Class to £1.35
stories.summary: Royal Mail is set to raise stamp prices, with first-class stamps rising by 10p to £1.35 and second-class stamps also increasing by 10p. The move is expected to affect households and small businesses that rely on regular post.

stories.title: Royal Mail Expands with New Bigger Hubs and Larger Parcel Fleets
stories.summary: Royal Mail is investing in new, larger sorting hubs and expanded parcel fleets to handle growing package volumes. The expansion reflects the ongoing shift from letters to parcels as e-commerce continues to grow.

stories.title: Second Class Mail Delivery Times Stretch to 12 Days
stories.summary: Royal Mail's second class mail is now reportedly taking up to 12 days to deliver letters in some cases, a significant slowdown from the standard 2-3 day target. Consumer complaints are rising amid the changes to delivery infrastructure.
